channel.title: Mcp on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in Mcp on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: github: MCP allowlists in enterprise managed settings
item.description:
GitHub added enterprise-managed settings to centrally control which MCP servers GitHub Copilot clients can run. Enterprise owners can now use allowedMcpServers and deniedMcpServers to allowlist or block specific MCP servers.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: Agent skills and MCP now generally available
item.description:
Copilot code review now generally supports agent skills and MCP servers for all Copilot Pro, Pro+, Business, and Enterprise users. These features have moved from public preview to general availability.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Announcing v2.0 of the official MCP C# SDK
item.description:
The official MCP C# SDK v2.0 now implements the 2026-07-28 MCP specification. It adds a stateless-first protocol, standardized HTTP headers, and Multi Round-Trip Requests for interactive tools while remaining backward compatible.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot for JetBrains adds improved OpenTelemetry configuration and model management
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now includes improved OpenTelemetry configuration and model management. The update also adds support for connecting MCP servers and custom agents in Claude agent flows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Analyze MSBuild Binary Logs with Copilot in VS Code
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the MSBuild Binlog Analyzer for VS Code, a Copilot-powered tool for reading MSBuild binary logs, explaining build failures, suggesting fixes, comparing builds, and identifying regressions. It uses the Microsoft.AITools.BinlogMcp MCP server.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub MCP Server supports the next MCP specification
item.description:
GitHub MCP Server will support the upcoming MCP spec ahead of its official release. The key protocol change is a move to a stateless core on 28 July 2026.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Building Agents that Act on Your Behalf with Toolboxes in Foundry
item.description:
Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry are presented as a way to let agents act on a user’s behalf while handling delegated identity across tools and services. The post highlights using a private Entra-protected MCP server alongside Microsoft’s managed Work IQ MCP server in the same agent flow.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — June update
item.description:
June 2026’s Visual Studio Copilot update focuses on usage visibility, a new trust layer for MCP servers, and the first C++ scenarios. The post emphasizes controls and clarity rather than new broad functionality.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Codex as agent provider and agentic enhancements in JetBrains IDEs
item.description:
GitHub added Codex as a new agent provider in public preview. JetBrains IDE updates also include Hooks support in the Customizations editor, richer MCP server management, and custom model support via configuration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: MCP Beyond the Chat Window: Build Diagnostics in CI
item.description:
Microsoft’s .NET blog describes using Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools for build diagnostics in CI, including the full Binlog MCP toolset and how it runs in a GitHub Actions workflow. It also reports evaluation data on efficiency gains from this approach.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: security: Securing AI agents: When AI tools move from reading to acting
item.description:
The post explains MCP tool poisoning as an attack that can turn trusted AI agents into a control plane for data loss. It describes how attackers manipulate tool descriptions to induce unauthorized actions, and outlines detection, containment, and prevention approaches.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: AutoJack: How a single page can RCE the host running your AI agent
item.description:
Microsoft describes AutoJack, an exploit chain where a single malicious webpage can cause remote code execution on the host running an AI browsing agent. The attack abuses localhost trust, missing authentication, and unsafe parameter handling in AutoGen Studio’s MCP WebSocket.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Detecting Duplicate Issues – Public Preview and issue fields MCP support for GitHub Issues
item.description:
GitHub Issues adds duplicate issue detection in public preview and expands MCP support for issue fields. The change is aimed at reducing duplicate triage work for maintainers, especially in large repositories.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: AI-Powered MSBuild Investigation with the Microsoft Binlog MCP Server
item.description:
Microsoft introduced the Binlog MCP Server for investigating MSBuild build failures and performance issues with AI. It provides 15 specialized tools for analyzing MSBuild binary logs through an AI assistant.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Agent finder for GitHub Copilot now available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes agent finder, a feature for selecting which MCP servers, skills, canvases, agents, and tools an agent should use. GitHub says it reduces the need to manually wire these components and helps avoid filling the context window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: MCP Server Knowledge Source in Microsoft Foundry IQ
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry IQ now supports external MCP servers as federated knowledge sources in public preview. This lets teams connect sources from systems like Salesforce, Atlassian, and Confluence without indexing all data themselves.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: MCP toolkit for Azure DocumentDB
item.description:
Azure DocumentDB adds support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in public preview. The MCP toolkit lets AI agents and LLM-powered apps connect directly to a DocumentDB database for natural-language querying and document retrieval.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure API Center now provides a data plane MCP server for enterprise-wide discovery of APIs and AI assets.
item.description:
Azure API Center now includes a data plane MCP server in general availability for enterprise-wide discovery of APIs and AI assets. The update is aimed at helping developers and agents find and connect to enterprise MCP servers, tools, APIs, and AI assets more easily.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure API Management now supports content safety controls for MCP and A2A APIs.
item.description:
Azure API Management is now generally available with content safety controls for MCP and A2A APIs. It is intended to help organizations apply consistent safety and compliance policies across agent interactions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Functions now supports hosting MCP Apps
item.description:
Azure Functions now generally supports hosting MCP apps. The update notes that MCP servers can use richer interactions beyond plain text, including visual data exploration, complex configuration, real-time status monitoring, and multi-step workflows.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Logic Apps MCP Server.
item.description:
Azure Logic Apps MCP Server is now generally available, aimed at making existing workflows callable by AI agents and MCP-based tooling without building custom API layers. The update focuses on reducing integration plumbing and operational complexity.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Data API builder with built-in GitHub Copilot in MSSQL extension
item.description:
The MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code now generally available includes Data API builder with built-in GitHub Copilot integration. It supports guided generation of REST, GraphQL, and Model Context Protocol back ends in the development workflow.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Announcing Agent Governance Toolkit MCP Extensions for .NET
item.description:
Microsoft announced a public preview .NET package for MCP servers that adds governance features through a single builder extension. The package includes policy enforcement, startup tool scanning, fallback governance, and response sanitization.

  • Source: .NET
